The CNN Fear & Greed Index ended the week at 22.1 (Extreme Fear), down from 26.2 (Fear) a week earlier. It fell to 19.4 on Monday, the lowest since October 23rd, and nearly matched that Thursday (20.0) before Friday’s bounce.

Four of the seven indicators are now in Extreme Fear, up from two, with two in Fear and one Neutral.

Extreme Greed = None
Greed = None
Neutral = stock price breadth (McClellan Volume Summation Index) (from Fear)
Fear = stock price strength (net new 52-week highs); junk bond demand (vs investment grade)
Extreme Fear = market momentum (SPX vs 125-DMA); put/call options (5-day put/call ratio) (from Fear); market volatility (VIX & its 50-DMA) (from Fear); safe haven demand (20-day difference in stock/bond returns)

BREAKING: 221 US trucking companies have filed for bankruptcy so far in 2026, on track for the highest annual total in 23 years.

This marks the 3rd consecutive year with at least 220 bankruptcies.

By comparison, annual bankruptcies were below 100 in both 2021 and 2022.

Furthermore, ~66% of small US trucking firms, typically operating 20 or fewer trucks, reported flat or declining revenue YoY, according to a Truckstop and Bloomberg survey of hundreds of carriers.

At the same time, ~40% expect to leave the industry or are unsure of their future over the next 6 months.

This comes as surging diesel prices, rising insurance premiums, and higher interest rates are increasingly squeezing smaller trucking companies.

The US trucking industry needs help.

BREAKING: US data center construction spending jumped +90% YoY in September, to a record annualized rate of $96.5 billion.

This also marks the largest YoY increase in 10 years.

This figure is now risen more than +60% YoY for 4 consecutive months.

Since the start of 2024, data center construction spending has nearly quadrupled.

Meanwhile, general office construction spending fell -8% YoY in September, to $46.0 billion, near its lowest level since January 2016.

This brought the gap between data center and general office construction spending to a record $50.5 billion.

Overall, US construction spending fell -1.9% MoM in September, its biggest monthly decline since April 2020.

The AI infrastructure buildout is transforming the US economy.

The global rate hike cycle is accelerating:

~45% of global central banks have raised interest rates over the last 3 months, the largest total in 3 years.

This proportion has surged +40 percentage points since March.

By comparison, between 2024 and March 2026, more central banks were cutting rates than raising them.

Furthermore, global central banks have delivered 42 rate hikes over the last 6 months, the largest number since late 2023.

This figure has quadrupled over the last 7 months and is comparable to the rate hike cycle seen in 2019.

The global monetary tightening cycle is gaining momentum.

BREAKING: The US unemployment rate has remained below 5.0% for 62 consecutive months, its 2nd-longest streak on record.

This trails only the 64-month stretch recorded during the 1960s and 1970s.

This is also 20 months longer than the 42-month streak that ended during the 2020 pandemic.

The current run began in September 2021, when the unemployment rate fell to 4.7%, from 5.1% in August 2021.

To put this into perspective, the unemployment rate has averaged 5.6% since the start of the century.

The US job market is still remarkably resilient.
